To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we validated the performance of 3 rapid diagnostic tests for detection of rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis and analyzed the probe reactions of these tests in detail.

we have validated the results of 3 commercially available RDTs against 34 unique rbpO mutations and have proposed a novel approach that uses these results for potential real-time evaluation of TB transmission.

we propose a novel approach to facilitate comparison between different TB diagnostics and shared test results, and that this is evidenced by the potential use of probe reactions for real-time evaluation and investigation of RR-TB outbreaks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of connected diagnostics and readily-available test results to facilitate real-time surveillance of drug-resistant TB transmission.
the use of digital TB diagnostics and test results in the context of TB surveillance and control, with the ultimate aim of reducing the global burden of RR-TB and, eventually, of TB.
the development of a new method for real-time evaluation and investigation of RR-TB cases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides a novel approach that has the potential to facilitate the detection of RR-TBs through the integration with a connectivity platform.
the potential of connected diagnostics for real-time surveillance of TB transmission has been proven, but it is yet to be realized.
our study provides evidence that the potential application of connected TB diagnostics and associated test result for real-time surveillance of RR-TB is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the potential use of digitally linked TB diagnostics is to accelerate efforts to end TB.
, in the context of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, we are calling for a paradigm shift from the traditional paper-based TB surveillance to real-time, digitally linked TB surveillance.
the use of connected TB diagnostics and associated test result data can be a game changer in TB surveillance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of RDTs in RR-TB surveillance is not a black box, as the probe reactions of the RDTs are not random.
we have demonstrated the value of using connected diagnostics and readily-available test results to evaluate transmission of drug-resistant TB.
the potential of connectivity solutions is not yet realized.
